title: Mixtures
description: A mixture is made by combining two or more materials. The materials in a mixture do not chemically change — they can often be separated again.

exercises.question: What is a MIXTURE?
choices: a brand-new substance made by a chemical reaction
two or more materials combined without chemically changing
exercises.exp: A mixture is two or more things combined. Each part keeps its own properties and can often be separated!

exercises.question: Which of these is a MIXTURE?
exercises.exp: Trail mix is a mixture — you can pick out the nuts, raisins, and seeds separately!

exercises.question: Salt dissolved in water is a ___.
exercises.exp: Salt water is a mixture — the salt and water do not chemically combine. You can evaporate the water to get the salt back!

exercises.question: How could you SEPARATE sand from water?
choices: by filtering through a cloth or paper
exercises.exp: Sand particles are large enough to be caught by a filter — the water passes through but the sand stays!

exercises.question: Which is NOT a mixture?
exercises.exp: Pure distilled water is a single substance (H₂O). Lemonade, soil, and air are all mixtures of different things.

exercises.question: Air is a mixture of gases. Which gases are in air?
choices: mainly nitrogen and oxygen, with other gases
exercises.exp: Air is about 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, and small amounts of other gases — a mixture!

exercises.question: You mix rice and beans. Is this a mixture?
choices: yes, you can still separate the rice from the beans
no, it creates a new substance
yes, but you cannot separate them
exercises.exp: Rice and beans in a bowl is a mixture — both stay the same and you can easily pick them apart.

exercises.question: How would you SEPARATE a mixture of iron filings and sand?
choices: using a magnet (iron is attracted, sand is not)
exercises.exp: A magnet pulls out the iron filings and leaves the sand behind — a clever separation method!

exercises.question: What property allows you to separate a mixture?
choices: the materials must look the same
the materials have different properties (size, magnetism, etc.)
they must be the same colour
they must be the same weight
exercises.exp: Different properties let you separate mixtures — size (filtering), magnetism, density (floating), or boiling point.

exercises.question: Soil is a mixture of ___.
choices: rock particles, minerals, water, air, and organic matter
exercises.exp: Soil is a complex mixture of tiny rock particles, minerals, water, air, and decomposed organic matter!

exercises.question: You have a mixture of peas and marbles. The BEST way to separate them is ___.
choices: filtering through a mesh that lets peas through but not marbles
exercises.exp: A mesh with holes sized between the peas and marbles would let peas fall through but hold back the marbles!

exercises.question: When you make ORANGE JUICE by squeezing oranges, the juice is ___.
choices: a mixture of water, sugars, acids, and vitamins
exercises.exp: Orange juice is a mixture of water, natural sugars, citric acid, vitamins, and many other compounds!

exercises.question: A HETEROGENEOUS mixture is one where you can SEE the different parts. Which is an example?
exercises.exp: In a tossed salad you can see the lettuce, tomatoes, cucumbers — each part is visible. Heterogeneous!

exercises.question: A HOMOGENEOUS mixture looks the same throughout. Which is an example?
exercises.exp: Salt water looks the same everywhere — you cannot see separate parts. It is a homogeneous mixture (a solution)!

exercises.question: How could you get the SALT back from salt water?
choices: by evaporating the water — the salt will be left behind
exercises.exp: Evaporate the water and the salt crystals are left behind — proving salt and water were just a mixture, not a new substance!

exercises.question: Which is the best method to separate a mixture of LARGE STONES and SAND?
choices: using a sieve or screen with holes
exercises.exp: A sieve with holes larger than sand but smaller than stones lets sand fall through and holds back the stones!

exercises.question: Lemonade is a mixture. Which of these is NOT one of its ingredients?
exercises.exp: Lemonade is a mixture of water, lemon juice, and sugar. Iron is a metal — definitely not in lemonade!

exercises.question: Can the parts of a mixture be SEPARATED without a chemical reaction?
choices: yes — using physical methods like filtering, sieving, or evaporating
no — only a chemical reaction can separate them
exercises.exp: Mixtures can always be separated by physical means — no chemical reaction needed. Just filtering, magnets, or evaporation!

exercises.question: Granite rock is a mixture of minerals (quartz, feldspar, mica). It is a ___ mixture.
choices: homogeneous — it looks the same everywhere
heterogeneous — you can see the different coloured speckles
exercises.exp: Look at granite closely — you can see different coloured crystals of quartz, feldspar, and mica. Heterogeneous!

exercises.question: You mix oil and water together and shake the bottle. After a moment, they ___.
choices: separate into two layers — oil floats on top of water
exercises.exp: Oil and water don't mix — oil is less dense so it floats on top of water. They separate naturally!

exercises.question: Muddy water is a mixture. How would you CLEAN it?
choices: by filtering it through sand or a paper filter to remove the mud particles
exercises.exp: Filtering removes mud particles — water passes through the filter but the mud stays behind. This is how water is cleaned!

exercises.question: Which of these is a pure SUBSTANCE (not a mixture)?
exercises.exp: Pure gold contains only gold atoms — it is a pure substance. Air, seawater, and milk are all mixtures!

exercises.question: A fruit salad has apples, bananas, and grapes. You want only the grapes. This is ___.
choices: separating a mixture — you just pick out the grapes
a chemical reaction — you must dissolve the other fruits
exercises.exp: Picking out the grapes is a simple physical separation — no chemical reaction needed. Mixtures are easy to separate!

exercises.question: Concrete is a mixture of sand, gravel, cement, and water. After hardening, concrete ___.
choices: can be easily separated back into its parts
forms a very hard material — the parts are difficult to separate
exercises.exp: Hardened concrete is extremely difficult to separate — a chemical reaction occurred as it set, making it more than just a mixture!

exercises.question: Which everyday mixture is SEPARATED by the method of letting it settle?
choices: muddy water — mud settles to the bottom
exercises.exp: If you leave muddy water, the mud particles slowly sink and settle to the bottom — separation by settling!

exercises.question: The air we breathe is a mixture. Which gas makes up about 21% of air?
exercises.exp: Oxygen makes up about 21% of air. Nitrogen makes up about 78%. We breathe in both, but only use the oxygen!

exercises.question: You have a mixture of paper clips and buttons. What is the FASTEST way to separate them?
choices: sort by hand one by one
use a magnet — it will attract the metal paper clips but not the plastic buttons
exercises.exp: A magnet attracts iron paper clips but not plastic buttons — quick and easy magnetic separation!

exercises.question: Seawater is a mixture. Which BEST describes it?
choices: a pure substance of water only
a mixture of water, salt, and other dissolved minerals
exercises.exp: Seawater contains dissolved salts, minerals, and gases — it is a complex homogeneous mixture!

exercises.question: In a mixture, do the ingredients REACT with each other chemically?
choices: no — in a mixture the ingredients keep their own properties
exercises.exp: In a mixture, ingredients keep their own properties and do NOT chemically react — that is what makes it a mixture!

exercises.question: Blood is a mixture. It contains red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets, and plasma. Scientists can separate these using ___.
choices: a centrifuge (fast spinning separates by density)
exercises.exp: A centrifuge spins blood at high speed — heavier parts (red blood cells) settle at the bottom, lighter plasma stays on top!

exercises.question: Which method would you use to separate a mixture of ALCOHOL and WATER?
choices: distillation — heating to boil off the alcohol first, then condensing it
exercises.exp: Distillation uses different boiling points — alcohol boils at 78°C, water at 100°C. Heat the mixture and collect each separately!

exercises.question: A mixture of sand and water can be separated by ___.
exercises.exp: Filter paper has tiny holes that let water through but trap sand particles. Filtering separates insoluble solids from liquids!

exercises.question: Iron filings mixed with sand can be separated using ___.
choices: a magnet — it pulls out the iron filings
exercises.exp: Iron is magnetic so a magnet attracts and removes iron filings from the sand. Easy and effective!

exercises.question: Salt dissolved in water forms a ___.
exercises.exp: Salt dissolved in water is a homogeneous mixture (solution) — the salt spreads evenly so you cannot see separate parts.

exercises.question: You can see separate layers in a bottle of salad dressing (oil and vinegar). This is a ___.
exercises.exp: Salad dressing is heterogeneous — oil and vinegar do not mix evenly and separate into visible layers!

exercises.question: What name is given to the solid that is left on filter paper after filtering?
exercises.exp: The residue is the solid left on the filter paper. The liquid that passes through is called the filtrate.

exercises.question: The liquid that passes THROUGH filter paper during filtration is called the ___.
exercises.exp: The filtrate is the liquid that passes through the filter. If you are filtering muddy water, the clear water is the filtrate.

exercises.question: Dissolving is different from melting because ___.
choices: dissolving requires a solvent (liquid) and produces a solution; melting just requires heat
exercises.exp: Dissolving needs a liquid solvent — sugar dissolves IN water. Melting is about changing state using heat — no solvent needed.

exercises.question: Which of these is a SUSPENSION (settles if left alone)?
exercises.exp: Orange juice with pulp is a suspension — the pulp particles are not truly dissolved and will settle to the bottom over time.

exercises.question: Air is a mixture of gases. The most abundant gas in air is ___.
exercises.exp: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of air — it is the most abundant gas. Oxygen is about 21%, and other gases fill the rest.

exercises.question: What does it mean when a substance is SOLUBLE?
choices: it dissolves in a liquid (usually water)
exercises.exp: Soluble means it dissolves — it breaks up evenly in a liquid. Sugar and salt are soluble in water.

exercises.question: Sand does NOT dissolve in water. Sand is ___.
exercises.exp: Sand is insoluble in water — it does not break up or dissolve. It just sits at the bottom or stays suspended briefly.

exercises.question: Which process would you use to get SALT back from salt water?
choices: evaporation — heat the water so it evaporates, leaving salt crystals
exercises.exp: Salt cannot evaporate, but water can! Evaporate the water away and you are left with dry salt crystals.

exercises.question: Granite rock is a mixture of minerals (quartz, feldspar, mica). Granite is ___.
choices: a heterogeneous mixture — you can see the different minerals
exercises.exp: Granite is heterogeneous — you can see the different coloured mineral grains (speckles) with the naked eye!

exercises.question: A SOLUTION is a type of mixture where ___.
choices: you can see all the parts clearly
one substance dissolves evenly in another — it looks the same throughout
the parts are all the same size
exercises.exp: A solution is a homogeneous mixture — everything is evenly spread. Salt water and air are both solutions.

exercises.question: You add more and more salt to water until no more dissolves. The solution is now ___.
choices: saturated — it cannot hold any more dissolved salt
exercises.exp: When no more solute can dissolve, the solution is saturated. The water has held as much salt as it possibly can!

exercises.question: Which is the BEST way to make sugar dissolve FASTER in water?
choices: stir the water and use warm water
exercises.exp: Stirring increases contact between sugar and water molecules; warm water gives more energy to break down sugar — both speed up dissolving!

exercises.question: Concrete is a mixture of cement, sand, gravel, and water. Once it hardens, can the ingredients be separated again?
choices: yes — add water to dissolve it
no — hardening concrete is a chemical change; the ingredients cannot be recovered by simple separation
exercises.exp: Hardened concrete involves chemical reactions — the ingredients are chemically bonded and cannot be separated by physical means.

exercises.question: A COLLOID is a type of mixture where tiny particles are permanently suspended. Which is a colloid?
choices: milk (tiny fat droplets suspended in water)
exercises.exp: Milk is a colloid — tiny fat droplets are so small they stay permanently suspended and do not settle. That is why milk looks white!

exercises.question: Which pair of liquids would NOT mix and would form layers?
exercises.exp: Oil and water do not mix — oil is less dense and floats on top of water forming two separate layers. They are immiscible!

exercises.question: What does the word SOLUTE mean in a solution?
choices: the liquid that does the dissolving
exercises.exp: The solute is what gets dissolved. In salt water, salt is the solute. The liquid doing the dissolving (water) is the solvent.
